Welcome
to Wendell Park Primary School
We recognise parents, carers and the wider family as children's first educators. The values that we share are the foundation stones upon which Wendell Park is built.
We work hard to provide a curriculum which inspires children's curiosity; develops their skills and fosters an understanding of others and the world about them.
Central to each child's learning is the growth of each child to be independent, confident and thoughtful. We want to inspire our children to be the best person they can be; to celebrate their achievements and contribute positively to the school community.
Wendell Park works closely with Brackenbury Primary School and Kenmont Primary School within a partnership arrangement sharing an Executive Head teacher. The partnership enables our staff to work collaboratively and share expertise with other teachers for the benefit of the Wendell Park children. We look forward to welcoming you to Wendell Park Primary School.
David Collins, Executive Head teacher of the Brackenbury, Kenmont and Wendell Park Primary School Federation.

pageCache.text:
Values & Ethos
Values & Ethos
We aim to be an outstanding, values-based school at the heart of our culturally diverse community, striving for excellence, enabling our children to achieve their highest potential in all areas of the curriculum.
Values
At Wendell our core values are:
Confidence: We believe that high self-esteem, self-confidence and happiness are central to our work.
Celebration: We believe in valuing and celebrating diversity and respect for all.
Challenging: We believe that our high expectations will lead to personal achievements and success that is right for all.
Caring: We believe in safety and support for every individual.
Cooperation: We are committed to working cooperatively for the good of the whole community.
School Vision Statement
Wendell Park Primary School will be viewed as one of the top 10% performing schools in England; where all children realise their potential. In an environment of creativity and critical thinking, they realise their individual talents and skills. Through nurturing relationships they grow in confidence to be aspirational life-long learners.
Core Purpose Statement
Wendell Park Primary School is built upon the values of a diverse and inclusive community. Our core purpose is to inspire a love of learning and sow the seeds of high achievement for all children, enabling them to thrive and grow to be happy, healthy citizens of the future. We do this through providing an ambitious and creative education which motivates our children to learn and be proud of their individuality.
For further information about how we promote these principles at Wendell Park please click below:
Social DevelopmentMoral Development Cultural DevelopmentSpiritual Development
Parent comments about Wendell Park School:
A wonderfully inclusive school. My children highly recommend it.
Wendell Park Primary is a great community school. Its children are fantastically diverse and its staff are wonderfully enthusiastic. We are very proud to be parents of the school.
Our daughter is happy and thriving at Wendell Park. We are really impressed by how quickly she is learning and developing, and also by all the exciting extra-curricular activities. Last week she was handling a python in class!
Wendell Park has an exceptional PTA group – come and get involved!
Wendell Park is a great school. Our daughter is learning, has lots of friends and is happy at the start and end of the school day. What more could you want?!
Learning Powers
At Wendell Park we are committed to developing lifelong learners who are excited by the prospect of learning something new.
Our world is for ever changing. The children of tomorrow will be expected to adapt frequently to changes in their personal lives and in the world of work. It is predicted that many of the jobs that will be available for future generations do not even exist yet.
In light of this, children need to develop the right attitudes and skills to manage change and thrive. To assist children with this development we have created The Wendell Learning Powers:
Based on the work of Professor Guy Claxton and the idea that we are all capable of becoming better learners
We want children to develop the Wendell Learning Powers in order for them to be effective learners who are able rise to challenges, learn from mistakes and work collaboratively with others. Wendell Park wants children to continually learn, develop and succeed.

pageCache.text:
SMSC & British Values
SMSC & British Values
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural (SMSC) Provision
At Wendell Park Primary School, spiritual, moral, social and cultural education underpin all aspects of school life. This work is absolutely integral to everything we do. It plays a significant role in contributing to the high levels of motivation, tolerance and excellent that the children demonstrate at our school.
The individuality of each child is valued and respected in order that:
This is not a “subject” in itself but opportunities to promote it are actively planned for across all subject areas of the curriculum; within collective worship; within our behaviour policy, within our safeguarding policy and within everything we do. It has particularly strong links to our work in Personal, Social and Health Education and Religious Education.
Definitions of terms
Spiritual development is the growth of insights, beliefs, attitudes and values which guide and motivate us. Through spiritual development, children can gain a sense of identity, their own self-worth and broader meaning and purpose in life.
Moral development is the building of a framework of moral values which control our personal behaviour. There is a recognition within this area of development that in a multi-racial, multicultural and multi-faith democracy such as Britain there will always be debate about moral values and these will differ from person to person.
Social development is concerned with the each child’s ability to develop the skills, understanding and personal qualities necessary for living and functioning effectively in our multi-racial, multicultural and multi-faith society and to be able to contribute to that society.
Cultural development is the about helping children to understand their own cultural heritage alongside the cultural traditions of the school, the local community, those of the wider British community and the wider world. They will explore these different cultures in order that they are able to understand, accept, respect and celebrate the differences and similarities they discover.
British Values
The DfE have reinforced the need “To create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
Wendell Park Primary School is committed to serving its community and surrounding areas. It recognises the multi-cultural, multi-faith and ever-changing nature of the United Kingdom, and therefore those it serves. It also understands the vital role it has in ensuring that groups or individuals within the school are not subjected to intimidation or radicalisation by those wishing to unduly, or illegally, influence them.
Our school, accepts admissions from all those entitled to an education under British law. It follows the policies outlined by the governing body regarding equal opportunities, which guarantee that there will be no discrimination against any individual or group, regardless of faith, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, political or financial status, or similar.
The Government emphasises that schools are required to ensure that key ‘British Values’ are taught in all UK schools. The government set out its definition of British values in the departmental advice entitled ‘Promoting Fundamental British Values as part of SMSC’ – DfE November 2014 which links to the ‘Prevent Duty’ – DfE June 2015 that requires all schools to have “due regard to the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism”.
The fundamental British Values that schools should have regard to are those of:
Democracy
The rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect

School Federation
School Federation
The Federation– Brackenbury, Kenmont and Wendell Park Primary School Federation
Wendell Park is a member of the Brackenbury, Kenmont and Wendell Park Primary School Federation. Since September 2014, Kenmont and Wendell Park Primary schools have operated with a shared Executive Head teacher. In September 2021, the partnership expanded with Brackenbury Primary School joining. The Federation is led by Executive Head teacher, Dave Collins. In April 2023 the informal partnership changed to a Federation.
Each of the schools is a LA maintained community school and each school has its own unique identity. We aspire for our schools to be the number one choice for their local community, because they provide a broad, engaging and fun education.
The shared aims of our federation are:
Working closely together with the Executive Head teacher, the schools benefit from: distributed leadership model, strong subject leadership, a rigorous cycle of innovation and staff development, and a community committed to our shared values.

English - Reading and Phonics
English - Reading and Phonics
Reading Intent
At Wendell Park, we aim to give all of our children the skills to listen and learn, and give them the confidence to express their own individual voice. We believe that nurturing proficient readers is a necessity in developing happy, independent and motivated life-long learners.
At Wendell Park, we understand that enthusiastic readers make proficient writers. We aim to model and nurture a love of reading and language, and to facilitate the safe space to play with words, acquire new vocabulary and to simply explore the effects of language.
Reading Implementation
At Wendell Park, fostering a love of reading underpins all of our learning. Throughout our school, we use dynamic book exploration and imaginative learning sequences to bring texts to life; we delve into high quality texts to explore and celebrate a range of authors, genres and cultures.
At Wendell Park, the foundations of reading are embedded in the early reader through the methodical teaching of phonics, subscribing to the Read Write Inc. model. At an early age, these fundamental skills are complimented by a love of story and book discovery: daily story times, habitual text exploration, stimulating story discussions and role-play of characters.
As our children continue on their journey, we provide reading lessons that delve into the seven Core Areas of Reading with directed activities and questioning; Vocabulary, Retrieval, Summary, Inference, Prediction, Compare & Contrast and Author Choice. We believe that good reading comprehension is a product of developing active readers that are enthusiastic and responsive, whilst given them the skills to verbalize their responses.
At Wendell Park we aim to bridge the gap between reading as a tool for learning and reading as a gateway to life! We provide timetabled storytelling and our adults help guide children to make reading choices that are accessible, appropriate and ambitious.
Reading Impact
Regardless of culture, background or ability, all of our children have access to high quality teaching and a rich range of text types. At Wendell Park, we are determined to create voracious readers that are ambitious, responsive and, above all, develop a life-long love of reading.

Governing Board
Brackenbury, Kenmont & Wendell Park Federaton Governing Board
We want to take this opportunity to introduce ourselves and the role we play at each school.
The Governing Board has an important part to play in raising school standards. We set the strategic direction for the schools, ensure financial accountability and monitor and evaluate school performance. While the Executive Head teacher and Heads of School are responsible for the day-to-day running of each school, our role is often described as acting as “a critical friend”. We provide strategic governance to ensure that all children get the best possible education, constantly challenging the schools to attain the best possible performance.
We have responsibility together with the leadership teams for agreeing the policies for the general running of each school. We fulfil statutory duties to ensure that each school is a safe, healthy and inclusive environment. We provide support and challenge to the leadership team of each school on all issues that affect the learning and welfare of our pupils. We also have a responsibility to handle complaints, though it is important to note that individual problems should, at the outset, be directed first to your child’s teacher and then to the school’s leadership team.
The governing Board is drawn from the school staff, parents of children at the schools, the community that our schools serve and people who have applied through – or been nominated by – the Local Authority. The usual term of office is four years but many governors stand for re-election and serve more than one term.
If you are interested in the work we do, would like to find out more, have any questions – or are interested in becoming a governor, please contact the school.
The full Governing Board meets once a term, and there are sub-committees dealing with Resources & Finance and Curriculum & Standards. Once approved, the Minutes of all our meetings are available from any school office.
Governing Board Membership and Appointing Bodies
The current and historical membership of the Governing Board can be viewed online at each schools 'Get Information About Schools' webpage which lists each governor's terms of office and appointing body. Pen Portraits of our current board can also be viewed at the bottom of this page. Brackenbury - Get Information About SchoolsKenmont - Get Information About SchoolsWendell Park Get Information About Schools
Governing Board Diversity Information
Diversity is important and the DfE want governing boards to be increasingly reflective of the communities they serve.
The DfE encourages schools to collect and publish governing board members’ diversity data. Board members can opt out of sharing their information, including protected characteristics, at any given time and so the information below may not include all members of the board.

Ms Wendi Webber
I have lived in Hammersmith and Fulham for 30+ years and I have been a governor for 17 years and a Chair of Governor's for 12 years. Both of my children attended Kenmont Primary School.
I am a professional musician and music teacher. I teach in the state and private sectors and I am passionate about making sure that our children in the state sector get as many opportunities and have as good outcomes as children in the private sector.
During the past few years I have seen the benefits of working in partnership with other schools and I am excited to see the further developments to come across each of the three schools in the federation .
Ms Anna Armstrong
Anna is an Assistant Head, (Higher Education and Careers) at Godolphin and Latymer School in Hammersmith where she has worked for over a decade.
Prior to becoming an Assistant Head, Anna has been the Head of History and Politics at both G&L and the John Lyon School in Harrow.
Anna studied for a BA Honours in History at the University of York before completing her PGCE at UCL IOE. She has undertaken UCL's Senior Leadership qualification and is a member of the Careers Development Institute.
Mandy Byrne
A resident of West London since university, I worked in primary education as a teacher, SENCo and Deputy Headteacher in the borough of Westminster for 27 years and moved to St Mary's University, Twickenham 10 years ago as a senior lecturer in primary education training teachers.
I have been a co-opted governor for a special needs specialist school as well as a staff governor in a mainstream primary school.
I am committed to the wellbeing and progress of all children with a particular interest in the support and development of children with special educational needs. I have trained as a dyslexia specialist teacher and a person-centred trainer focusing on the needs of individual children and working closely with their families.
Ms Alice Careless
Born and brought up in the local area, I was a pupil of Brackenbury in the 1980s. Both of my children have attended the school with my youngest moving on in July 2021. I joined as a parent governor in 2015 and was most recently the co-chair of governors at Brackenbury. I am a Co-opted governor. I have spent the last 24 years working in a number of local government and charitable organisations providing advice and advocacy for the local community. I am currently working for a national charity providing welfare advice, financial assistance and wellbeing support. ‹
Ms Ffion Cartwright
I've lived in Hammersmith and Fulham for the past three years and it's a place I'm proud to call home. I currently work as a Strategy Advisor in the Secretary of State for Housing, Policy and Strategy Unit, where I help drive forward long-term policy across government. My experience in public service-as well as my role as a proud aunty to two nieces- has given me a strong appreciation for the role that education plays in building confidence, nurturing potential and breaking down barriers to opportunity.
As one of the newest members of the governing board, I've thoroughly enjoyed getting to know the school, its staff, and the wider community. I'm excited to contribute to its continued success and support its strategic development in the years ahead.
Mr David Collins
I have been the head teacher at Brackenbury since September 2016 and Executive Head since September 2021. Prior to that I was a Head teacher of a primary school in Hampshire. I started my teaching career in 2001 in Hampshire and have taught and worked in a variety of Primary and Junior Schools. I enjoy working with governors in setting the strategic direction of the school and celebrating the schools achievements.
Ms Gilly Di Loreto
I've proudly called Hammersmith and Fulham home for nearly three decades, and my two sons are currently thriving at Wendell Park Primary School. In my day-to-day life, I work in the healthcare sector, where I help manage various services and provide support to those in need.
I'm genuinely eager to delve into the inner workings of our schools, discover how we can assist parents, and understand the steps we can take to support the growth and well-being of our children.

With a long career in digital media and tech, I am keenly interested in Responsible AI and the use of AI in education and see how, if used properly, it can expand horizons for all. Married, I make Brook Green my home.

Phonics / Communication and Language
Communication and Language
The development of children's spoken language underpins all seven areas of learning and development. Children's back-and-forth interactions, from an early age, form the foundations for language and cognitive development. The number and quality of the conversations they have with adults and peers throughout the day in a language-rich environment is crucial.
Below are some examples of the kinds of things we do in class to develop your child's communication and language skills:
* commenting on what children are interested in or doing and echoing back what they say with new vocabulary added
* reading frequently to children and engaging them actively in stories, non-fiction, rhymes and poems and then providing them with extensive opportunities to use and embed new words in a range of contexts will give children the opportunity to thrive.
* through conversation, story telling and role play, where children share their ideas with support and modelling from their teacher and sensitive questioning that invites them to elaborate, children become comfortable using a rich range of vocabulary and language structures.
If you would like any support with trying any of the above at home, or some further suggestions of activities, please speak to your child's teacher.

Remote Learning
Remote Learning
The school is committed to providing learning while children are isolating, or during any future partial school closures and local or national lockdowns.
The school will provide online learning and homework for the children through Google Classroom and a number of online subscriptions such as Maths and Spelling Shed, Times Tables Rockstars and Pearson’s Bug Club.
Communication with parents about learning can be addressed on Google Classroom and urgent or private matters should be directed to the school office email admin@wendellpark.lbhf.sch.uk

French
French
Intent (before the teaching)
At Wendell Park, we want to develop children’s experiences of language acquisition and encourage curiosity about languages and we do this by teaching French to all pupils in Key Stage 2.
We want children to develop their understanding of what they hear and read; to express themselves with confidence; to extend their knowledge of how language words and explore the differences between French and English.
Our ultimate aim is to strengthen our children’s sense of identity and foster an understanding of others and the world around them which we do through learning about cultures in Francophone countries and compare this to their own lived experiences.
Implementation (subject in action)
French is taught by a subject specialist teacher and all children access an hour of French teaching per week.
In French, children will learn to speak confidently, read fluently, write purposefully and understand the culture of the countries in which the language is spoken.
In conjunction with the National Curriculum for Languages, we aim to ensure that children:
Alongside embracing the National Curriculum programme of study, French teaching and learning at Wendell Park follows a cyclical methodology that incorporates and builds upon the core elements of speaking, listening, reading and writing. Each unit of work develops from speaking and listening – hearing the new vocabulary and being able to practise it with songs, rhymes and games; to being able to read the words and looking for phonics links and differences as well as similarities between English and French. This is followed by writing the words in meaningful contexts (linking the units to the lives of the children and their surroundings for example). Understanding is then assessed through questioning, thumbs up/down, written activities and formal assessment at the completion of each unit.
Impact (after the teaching)
Assessment in French is through ‘Assessment for Learning’ techniques which support the teacher in planning for future lessons.
During the unit of work, the teacher makes a judgement against the National Curriculum statements and our Knowledge and Skills Progression, as to whether the child has achieved, is above or below expected standards.
Children can demonstrate their understanding at the end of a topic through a mini assessment which allows the children to show what they have learnt.
Children at Wendell Park have an appreciation for language acquisition. They are keen learners both of the language and also of culture. Year 6 pupils are prepared for the next step of their learning whether this will continue to be in French or whether they will implement the skills they have learnt at Wendell Park to a new language.
